# The SpaceX IPO: Science Fiction or Serious Investment? | The Weekly Wrap

First listed: 2026-05-29 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The SpaceX IPO: Science Fiction or Serious Investment? | The Weekly Wrap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nEIndpBgYQ) - 2026-05-29
- [Substack: The SpaceX IPO: Science Fiction or Serious Investment? | The Weekly Wrap](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) - 2026-05-29

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Recorded May 28 and published May 29, this wrap challenges SpaceX proposed valuation using segment economics, index mechanics and a comparison with established technology businesses. It also discusses Salesforce accounting, Dell demand and the contrasting economics of banks and ratings agencies.

The segment-level skepticism and insistence on treating stock compensation as a real cost are useful. The claim that Nasdaq conspired to guarantee success is not established, and the float cap is described without its full-cap weighting context. Bank of America margin improvement regardless of Fed policy is also too categorical.

## Material claims

<a id="substack-202957175-c001"></a>
### 001. AI providers subsidize adoption and token costs are beginning to rise, especially for agentic use.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:12-1:27](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Costs and subsidies vary by vendor, model, workload and contract. A broad claim needs a matched pricing and cost series.

Assessment test: Compare price per completed task, compute costs and free allowances.

[Source at 2:22-2:39](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The geopolitical status and market interpretation are not causally identified by a rising index.

<a id="substack-202957175-c003"></a>
### 003. A sweeping SpaceX mission and speculative businesses do not by themselves justify the proposed valuation.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 2:53-4:03](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is valuation discipline, not a forecast that ambitious projects will necessarily fail.

Assessment test: Model probability-weighted cash flows, financing and dilution.


<a id="substack-202957175-c004"></a>
### 004. Nasdaq changed its rules to favor SpaceX, with rapid entry and triple float weighting.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 4:09-5:10](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The general methodology change and three-times-float cap exist, but the cap limits weighting relative to full capitalization. The public consultation and general eligibility rules do not establish conspiracy or guaranteed success.

Assessment test: Apply the actual methodology to shares, float, liquidity and eligibility dates.

- [Nasdaq-100 methodology update](https://www.nasdaq.com/newsroom/nasdaq100-index-methodology-update-why-now) (2026-05-08): The May 1 change followed consultation, replaced the 10% minimum float requirement and added a general Fast Entry pathway for top-40-sized listings. The three-times-float mechanism is a cap relative to full capitalization, not evidence of a private agreement guaranteeing an IPO return.

<a id="substack-202957175-c005"></a>
### 005. A large retail allocation is intended to make SpaceX a cult stock, the only way its valuation can work.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | investment thesis | major

The intention and only-way claim are not established by the allocation alone. A valuation can be tested without assuming every retail investor motive.

Assessment test: Verify allocation terms and model cash-flow requirements under multiple scenarios.


<a id="substack-202957175-c006"></a>
### 006. SpaceX comprises launch, connectivity and AI businesses with very different economics.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 5:41-6:03](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The registration statement reports the three segments separately. Aggregating them can conceal their sharply different profitability and capital needs.

Assessment test: Analyze each segment before summing enterprise value.

- [SpaceX Form S-1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026036936/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm) (2026-05-20): The S-1 reports Q1 2026 revenue of $4.694 billion. Connectivity earned operating income of $1.188 billion; Space and AI lost $662 million and $2.469 billion. The combined operating loss was $1.943 billion, before interest and other items.

<a id="substack-202957175-c013"></a>
### 013. Salesforce adjusted earnings look much better than GAAP partly because stock compensation is excluded.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 11:13-12:36](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The release reports $2.42 GAAP versus $3.88 adjusted EPS. Stock compensation is an economic cost, though other adjustments also contribute to the difference.

Assessment test: Reconcile the complete adjustment bridge and share dilution.

- [Salesforce fiscal Q1 2027 results](https://investor.salesforce.com/news/news-details/2026/Salesforce-Delivers-Record-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027-Results/default.aspx) (2026-05-27): Revenue rose 13% including $444 million from Informatica; GAAP EPS was $2.42 versus adjusted $3.88. The adjustment bridge includes more than stock-based compensation.

<a id="substack-202957175-c016"></a>
### 016. Regulatory capital structurally caps bank return on equity at 12-15%.

**Wrong** | Maria, listener question | explanation | major

[Source at 13:40-13:58](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: reported | Horizon: not stated

The listener universal cap is contradicted by JPMorgan reported ROE of 17% in Q3 2025. This uses ROE itself, not the higher ROTCE figure. Regulatory capital constrains leverage but does not impose a universal 12-15% profitability ceiling.

Assessment test: Distinguish ROE from ROTCE and compare actual capital and earnings.

- [JPMorgan Chase Q3 2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/19617/000162828025044845/a3q25erfexhibit991narrative.htm) (2025-10-14): Reported firmwide ROE was 17%, while ROTCE was separately reported at 20%. The ROE figure itself exceeds a claimed universal 15% ceiling.

The listener explanation requires dated total returns and issuance composition; total debt outstanding is not the same as fee-generating new issuance.

No horizon is specified. Healthy bank returns and a macro recession forecast are separate claims.

<a id="substack-202957175-c019"></a>
### 019. Bank of America low-yield securities rolling off should improve net interest margin over several years regardless of Fed policy.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 16:08-16:26](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: Several years after May 2026

Reinvestment can help, but deposit repricing, loan yields, mix and the rate path can offset that benefit. Regardless of policy is stronger than the balance-sheet mechanism supports.

Conditional reasoning: Higher asset yield can be offset by a greater increase in funding cost or a change in asset mix. One side of the balance sheet cannot guarantee margin direction under every rate path.

Assessment test: Model asset and liability repricing jointly under alternative curves.


<a id="substack-202957175-c020"></a>
### 020. Ratings-agency oligopoly and recovering issuance make Moody and S&P attractive.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | investment thesis | major

[Source at 16:28-16:47](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The investment view lacks a price target or horizon. A concentrated industry can still be overvalued or exposed to issuance cycles.

Assessment test: Track ratings volume, fee yield, recurring analytics and valuation.


<a id="substack-202957175-c021"></a>
### 021. Ratings agencies compromised standards for structured-finance fees before the GFC, but new management resolves the ownership concern.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 16:48-17:06](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-spacex-ipo-science-fiction-or) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

FCIC supports incentive conflicts and rating failures. Whether management change resolves an investor ethical objection is normative and does not prove every incentive has disappeared.

Assessment test: Separate historical findings, current governance and personal ethical criteria.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01-27): Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

## Framework and tools

- Read the S-1 rather than rely on a mission statement.
- Separate current profitable segments from speculative addressable markets.
- Use comparable growth and margins alongside valuation.
- Treat stock compensation and funding needs as economic costs.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- S-1 segment income and capex
- Price/sales comparisons
- TAM composition
- Index float and fast-entry rules
- GAAP/non-GAAP reconciliation
- ROTCE and net interest margin

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.
- Publisher transcript contains several genuine gaps and corrupted numerical phrases, including TAM and comparative multiples. Only clear recoverable claims are evaluated.
- Recorded Thursday May 28 for the May 29 wrap.
- The quoted SpaceX loss around $1.9 billion is operating loss, not the much larger loss before taxes; the transcript does not clearly specify the measure.
- The mailbag is abridged by the host; listener assertions are separated from his response.
